faq: Which payment providers can you work with?
Stripe is our most common choice, and we also work with Paddle, Lemon Squeezy and PayPal subscriptions. Tell us which you use. We set it up inside your own account.
Can you help me decide my prices?
We can share common ways to structure tiers and talk through your options, but we do not promise any price will increase sales. The final pricing decision is yours.
Can I change plans or prices later?
Yes. Existing subscribers normally stay on their current price while new customers get the new one. We explain how to do this safely and leave notes in your project.
Will my current subscribers be affected?
Not unless you ask. We add new plans beside existing ones and test on your provider's test mode first. Moving current customers is a separate task that we scope with you.

SaaS pricing plans and tiers setup in Stripe or a similar provider, built by Ecom Swift LLC. We turn your pricing idea into real products and prices, connect them to your app and show customers a clear choice before they pay.

## What does it mean to set up pricing plans?

Setting up pricing plans means creating each tier as a product in your payment provider, giving it monthly and yearly prices, and telling your app what each tier allows. The provider holds the billing side: names, prices, currencies and renewal periods. Your app holds the product side: seats, projects, exports or any other limit a plan controls.

These two sides must agree. If the pricing page says a plan includes five seats but the app allows ten, or the provider charges one amount while the page shows another, customers notice quickly and trust drops.

## Why plan structure shapes buying decisions

A pricing page is often the most visited page after the home page. Visitors compare tiers, look for the one that fits their size and check what changes between levels. Few plans with clear names make that comparison easy. Too many plans, vague limits or hidden extras make people hesitate or leave to ask a question first.

The technical setup also affects you later. Plans created with consistent names and identifiers are simple to change, report on and discount. Plans created ad hoc become a tangle after a year of experiments. Saving the plan identifier on each customer record lets your app check what that customer may do and lets your reports count customers by plan.

## What a good plan setup includes

- Each tier created as a product in your provider, with a clear name and description.
- Monthly and yearly prices for each tier.
- Optional add-on items, such as extra seats or extra storage.
- Regional prices in more than one currency, when you sell abroad.
- The plan identifier stored on every customer record.
- Feature limits per plan, such as seats, projects or exports.
- Checks in your app that read the plan before allowing a feature.
- A pricing table or page section for your website.
- A yearly discount presented honestly beside the monthly price.
- Test purchases for every plan, covering both billing periods.

## How we do it

You tell us the tiers, the prices and what each one includes. If you are unsure about prices, we can discuss structure, but the numbers remain your decision. We then create the products and prices in your provider account and connect them to your app. The Basic package creates a small set of plans with monthly and yearly prices and saves the plan on each customer. The Standard package adds a fuller tier ladder, limits that your product enforces, a pricing table for your website and test purchases for every plan. The Premium package adds add-on items, prices in several currencies, a clearly shown yearly discount and a designed pricing page section, followed by a handover call.

Existing subscribers are handled with care. Changing a price in a provider normally means creating a new price record, while current subscribers stay on the old one until you decide to move them. We explain the choice before touching anything that affects live customers.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Give each plan a name that describes who it is for.
- State limits in numbers customers can understand, such as seats or projects.
- Keep the same plan names in the provider, the app and the pricing page.
- Show the yearly saving clearly next to the monthly price.
- Test every plan with both billing periods.

**Avoid:**
- Creating a new plan for every customer request.
- Showing a price on the website that differs from the provider.
- Putting a feature behind a plan without enforcing it in the app.
- Changing prices for existing subscribers without telling them.
- Adding so many tiers that visitors cannot choose.

## Who this suits

This service suits a founder with a pricing idea on paper and no billing setup. It suits a product moving from one flat price to tiers with limits. It also suits a team preparing a new pricing page and wanting the provider and the app updated to match it.

## What we need and how to get going

Send a short description of each plan: its name, its monthly and yearly price, and what it includes. Tell us which provider you use and in which currencies you sell. We need developer or collaborator access to your app and a team role in your provider account, but never your passwords. After you order, we reply with a short checklist and share a test link for you to try each plan before it is live.
